title: Verify synthetic chunking and final token attribution for streaming sessions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: We have recurring discrepancies in billed token totals for streaming sessions when clients send partial chunks, abruptly close streams, or reconnect and retry. The meter currently assigns tokens at several points (on chunk emit, on finalization, and on reconnection replays). That has led to duplicated charges in cases where a client-side retry is indistinguishable from network-induced duplicate delivery, and to undercounts when the finalization event is dropped and synthetic chunking logic doesn't account for pending KV cache outputs.

Goal: Define and implement a deterministic policy for 'synthetic chunking' (the process we use to synthesize a final emitted chunk when streams close unexpectedly) and ensure final token attribution is both correct and idempotent. Avoid double charging across retries/reconnects while preserving accurate input vs. output accounting and quota enforcement.

Scope: billing path and metering pipeline components involved in streaming: gateway (session lifecycle), chunk sequencer, metering service (tokenizer + aggregator), and the accounting event store. Does NOT include non-streaming REST generation paths except where shared libraries are adjusted.

Problems to address:
- Partial output emission where the last partial chunk is not finalized and later re-emitted on reconnect leads to either double charge or undercount depending on finalization order.
- Retry/reconnect semantics: clients may resend the last N tokens; without a session-level idempotency key and chunk dedup rules we double-bill.
- Synthetic chunking heuristics: current heuristic produces synthetic final chunks based on timeouts which don't consider pending KV cache outputs or tokenization differences across model variants (e.g., tokenizer merges).
- Quota enforcement: mid-stream quota checks sometimes deny in-flight finalization events, leaving a session in an inconsistent accounting state.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Session-scoped sequence numbers + a per-session monotonic 'last_finalized_seq' persisted to the accounting event store at commit. All emitted chunk events must include seq numbers and a session id.
2) Introduce an idempotency token for client retries (supported via gateway header X-Stream-Idempotency). If missing, gateway generates a deterministic id based on session id + last_emitted_seq.
3) Synthetic-finalization RFC: define a deterministic synthetic final event generator that only emits when (a) no real-final event observed within timeout T, (b) last_emitted_seq > last_finalized_seq, and (c) there is a KV-cache-consistent token estimate. This synthetic event is marked with synthetic=true and uses a canonical tokenization path used for billing (same tokenizer binary/version as meter).
4) Metering commits must be atomic with finalization: when finalization (real or synthetic) is committed, the accounting store records input_tokens, output_tokens, and attribution metadata (seq range, synthetic flag, idempotency token). Downstream aggregation jobs will ignore duplicate commits with identical session+seq+idempotency triple.
5) Quota check path will consult the projected final token total (current committed + estimated remainder) and either allow final commit or return an explicit quota-exceeded terminal event that is also persisted (so clients know to stop).

Acceptance criteria (see field 'acceptance_criteria') and test plan are below. Implementation will be split into two PRs: one for schema + event store changes and test harness, another for gateway + metering runtime changes and integration tests.

Rollout strategy: feature-flag the synthetic finalization and idempotency handling behind runtime flags per-region. Start with staging + two Canary accounts, monitor diffs between previously billed totals and new totals for the same sessions (backfill comparison).

Risks and mitigations:
- Small tokenization mismatch across binaries: pin billing tokenizer binary in metering service and migrate in a controlled fashion.
- Race between real final and synthetic: sequence numbers and persisted last_finalized_seq avoid double-commit.
- Increased latency on finalization due to extra quota-check RPC: cache quota projections in gateway for hot sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Finalized events (real or synthetic) are persisted with session id, seq range, input_tokens, output_tokens, synthetic flag, and idempotency token.
Replays or duplicate finalization attempts with identical session+seq+idempotency do not create additional billed events (idempotent commit).
Staging load tests show <0.1% change in median p99 billing latency when synthetic finalization is enabled behind flag.
End-to-end integration tests reproduce previously observed double-charge case and demonstrate single, correct charge after the change.
Quota denial events are recorded and produce an auditable terminal record preventing orphan in-flight sessions.
Monitoring dashboards report no sustained upward billing discrepancies for canary accounts over a 72-hour window after rollout.
comments: 2026-03-01 Aisha K: Triage review done. Prior incidents show customers reporting 1-2% overbilling for long-lived streaming sessions. Punted to ENG billing team for investigation.

2026-03-03 Marco H: Investigated sample session logs (see attachment). Found cases where client reconnects re-emitted last chunk with different token boundaries causing mismatch in tokenizer-run counts.
Action: add deterministic tokenizer and embed tokenizer version in all chunk events.

2026-03-05 Marco H: PoC for session seq + idempotency token implemented. Local unit tests pass. Rough patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821 (draft). Need to harden commit atomicity with event-store transaction semantics.

2026-03-07 Diana L (Reviewer): Reviewed PR. Major comments: (1) ensure synthetic finalization timeout is configurable per-account; (2) add integration test that simulates network partition and replay; (3) add metric synthetic_finalizations_total and synthetic_finalization_dedup_rate.
2026-03-09 Marco H: Addressed review comments, added integration test harness in tests/streaming_metering_it.py. New PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4890 (ready for review).
2026-03-10 Aisha K: Approved design changes. Schedule rollout to staging on 2026-03-12 behind flag. Note: Coordinate with billing analytics to run delta queries on billed totals for canary accounts.
2026-03-10 Ops: Added checklist for monitoring: run backfill diff job (billing-diff-v2) after canary, monitor pager for spike in quota-denied sessions.
